# Sirach Chapter 4 — Disagreement Log

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Chapter:** Sirach 4 (31 verses)
**Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Total Disagreements:** 20

---

## Disagreement 001 — v.1: "empty eyes" vs. "waiting in suspense"

**EMET:** "do not make the needy wait with empty eyes"
**LOGOS:** "do not keep the needy waiting in suspense"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't keep desperate people waiting and hoping in vain"
**Issue:** Greek eis kenas elpidas = "into empty hopes." EMET's "empty eyes" is evocative but "empty eyes" isn't the Greek; "empty hopes" is. LOGOS "in suspense" is interpretive. Consensus: "do not keep the needy waiting with empty eyes" — retaining the vivid image while noting the Greek says "empty hopes."

---

## Disagreement 002 — v.2: "grieve the hungry" vs. "add to the grief of the hungry"

**EMET:** "Do not grieve the hungry"
**LOGOS:** "Do not add to the grief of the hungry"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't add to the misery of someone who is starving"
**Issue:** Greek mē epidē algēma nēstei = "do not show grief/pain to the hungry." LOGOS "add to the grief" is interpretive. EMET more literal. Consensus: "Do not add to the grief of the hungry."

---

## Disagreement 003 — v.3: "heart that is bitter" vs. "troubled heart"

**EMET:** "do not add trouble to a heart that is bitter"
**LOGOS:** "Do not make a troubled heart more bitter"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't pour salt into a bitter wound"
**Issue:** Greek kardias tethlymmenas = "a crushed/troubled heart." PNEUMA's "pour salt into a wound" is vivid but not in the Greek. Consensus: "do not make a troubled heart more bitter."

---

## Disagreement 004 — v.6: "his maker will hear" vs. "his Maker will hear"

**EMET:** "his maker will hear his prayer"
**LOGOS:** "his Maker will hear his prayer"
**PNEUMA:** "their Creator will hear that prayer"
**Issue:** PNEUMA shifts to plural "their." Greek ho ktisas auton = "the one who created him" — singular. Consensus: "his Maker will hear his prayer."

---

## Disagreement 005 — v.7: "make yourself beloved" vs. "gain the goodwill"

**EMET:** "Make yourself beloved in the congregation"
**LOGOS:** "Gain the goodwill of the assembly"
**PNEUMA:** "Win the respect of your community"
**Issue:** Greek euereston poiēson seauton synagōgē = "make yourself pleasing to the assembly." EMET "beloved" and LOGOS "goodwill" are both accurate. "Assembly" (synagōgē) is preferable to "congregation" (more neutral). Consensus: LOGOS reading.

---

## Disagreement 006 — v.8: "answer him with peaceful words" vs. "answer them with a gentle word"

**EMET:** "answer him with peaceful words with humility"
**LOGOS:** "answer them with a gentle word"
**PNEUMA:** "Answer them with gentleness and humility"
**Issue:** Greek en prautēti apokrithēti autō = "answer him in meekness." EMET adds "peaceful" which is not in the Greek. LOGOS loses "humility." Consensus: "answer them gently and humbly."

---

## Disagreement 007 — v.9: "wronged from the hand of the wrongdoer" vs. "victims from their oppressors"

**EMET:** "Deliver the wronged from the hand of the wrongdoer"
**LOGOS:** "Rescue the wronged from their oppressor"
**PNEUMA:** "Rescue victims from their oppressors"
**Issue:** Greek rhysai adikoumenon ek cheiros adikounta = "rescue the wronged from the hand of the wrongdoer." EMET is most literal. Consensus: LOGOS — "wronged/wrongdoer" pairing is more literal than "victims/oppressors."

---

## Disagreement 008 — v.10: "son of the Most High" vs. "child of the Most High"

**EMET:** "like a son of the Most High"
**LOGOS:** "like a child of the Most High"
**PNEUMA:** "like a child of the Most High"
**Issue:** Greek huios Hypsistou = "son of the Most High." Hebrew ben Elyon. EMET preserves the male-gendered Greek; LOGOS/PNEUMA gender-neutralize. Consensus: "child of the Most High" — inclusive; the text addresses both men and women.

---

## Disagreement 009 — v.11: "exalts her children" vs. "nurtures her children"

**EMET:** "Wisdom exalts her children"
**LOGOS:** "Wisdom nurtures her own children"
**PNEUMA:** "Wisdom is a mother to her children"
**Issue:** Greek hypsoi tekna autēs = "exalts her children." LOGOS "nurtures" is incorrect — the Greek says "exalts." PNEUMA changes the sentence entirely. Consensus: "Wisdom exalts her children and gives help to those who seek her."

---

## Disagreement 010 — v.13: "inherits glory" vs. "obtains glory"

**EMET:** "Whoever holds her fast inherits glory"
**LOGOS:** "Whoever holds fast to her obtains glory"
**PNEUMA:** "Whoever clings to her will be crowned with honor"
**Issue:** Greek klēronomei doxan = "inherits glory." EMET's "inherits" is correct. LOGOS "obtains" is weaker. PNEUMA changes the metaphor entirely. Consensus: "Whoever holds fast to her inherits glory."

---

## Disagreement 011 — v.15: "judge the nations" vs. "render judgment among the nations"

**EMET:** "will judge the nations"
**LOGOS:** "will give judgment among the nations"
**PNEUMA:** "will have the discernment to judge nations"
**Issue:** Greek krinei ethnē = "will judge nations." EMET is most literal. PNEUMA adds "discernment" without Greek support. Consensus: "will render judgment among the nations."

---

## Disagreement 012 — v.17: "tortuous paths" vs. "winding paths"

**EMET:** "she will walk with him on tortuous paths"
**LOGOS:** "she will lead him along winding paths"
**PNEUMA:** "she leads her students along steep and winding roads"
**Issue:** Greek hodos skolias = "crooked/twisted paths." EMET "tortuous" is strong but accurate. LOGOS "winding" is more neutral. PNEUMA adds "steep." Consensus: "winding paths."

---

## Disagreement 013 — v.17: "bring fear and cowardice upon him" vs. "bringing him fear and timidity"

**EMET:** "she will bring fear and cowardice upon him"
**LOGOS:** "bringing him fear and timidity"
**PNEUMA:** "She makes them anxious and afraid"
**Issue:** Greek phobēsei auton kai deiliasai = "will frighten him and make him timid." EMET "cowardice" is strong. LOGOS "timidity" is more neutral. Consensus: "bringing fear and timidity upon him."

---

## Disagreement 014 — v.18: "come back to him on the straight path" vs. "return to him on the straight way"

**EMET:** "she will come back to him on the straight path and will gladden him"
**LOGOS:** "she will return to him on the straight way and restore his joy"
**PNEUMA:** "she turns around and leads them back on the smooth path"
**Issue:** Greek eutheia = "straight." PNEUMA's "smooth" changes the meaning. Consensus: EMET/LOGOS — "straight path."

---

## Disagreement 015 — v.20: "watch for the right moment" vs. "watch for the opportune time"

**EMET:** "Watch for the right moment"
**LOGOS:** "Watch for the opportune time"
**PNEUMA:** "Watch your timing"
**Issue:** Greek phylaxon kairon = "guard the opportune moment." Both "right moment" and "opportune time" are accurate. Consensus: "Watch for the opportune moment."

---

## Disagreement 016 — v.21: "glory and favor" vs. "honor and favor"

**EMET:** "a shame that leads to glory and favor"
**LOGOS:** "shame that leads to honor and favor"
**PNEUMA:** "shame that leads to honor and grace"
**Issue:** Greek doxa = "glory/honor." EMET "glory"; LOGOS/PNEUMA "honor." Consensus: "glory and favor."

---

## Disagreement 017 — v.25: "speak against the truth" vs. "contradict the truth"

**EMET:** "Do not speak against the truth"
**LOGOS:** "Do not contradict the truth"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't argue against truth"
**Issue:** Greek kata tēs alētheias mē antikeisthai = "do not stand opposed to the truth." EMET and LOGOS are both accurate. Consensus: LOGOS.

---

## Disagreement 018 — v.26: "strive against the current of a river" vs. "try to stop a river"

**EMET:** "do not strive against the current of a river"
**LOGOS:** "do not try to stop a river with your hand"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't try to swim against an impossible current"
**Issue:** Greek kata rhous potamou = "against the current of a river." LOGOS adds "with your hand" (not in Greek). Consensus: "do not try to stop a river in flood."

---

## Disagreement 019 — v.28: "fight even unto death" vs. "fight to the death"

**EMET:** "Strive even unto death for the truth"
**LOGOS:** "Fight to the death for truth"
**PNEUMA:** "Fight for what is true, all the way to your last breath"
**Issue:** Greek heos thanatou = "until death." EMET "strive" (agōnisai); LOGOS "fight" is slightly more combative. Consensus: "Fight to the death for truth."

---

## Disagreement 020 — v.30: "suspicious of your servants" vs. "suspicious of your household"

**EMET:** "do not be suspicious of your servants"
**LOGOS:** "do not be suspicious toward your household"
**PNEUMA:** "Don't treat your own household like suspects"
**Issue:** Greek mē katanarkā = "do not be burdensome/oppressive." "Suspicious" is interpretive; the Greek is more about being overbearing. Consensus: "do not be overbearing toward your household."

---
